title: Precision-Latency-Utility Simulator — Proforma
content:
Purpose:
Short working worksheet for evaluating per-workload utility (quality) vs latency vs infra unit cost under various quantization regimes (FP16 baseline, FP8, INT8, 4-bit). Designed to be a lightweight calculator teams can clone and adapt to decide which quant profile to recommend for a given route or SLA.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Quantization reduces GPU memory footprint and increases effective throughput but can degrade output quality differently across workloads.
- This simulator expresses tradeoffs as: per-token unit-cost, median latency (p50/p95), and relative quality delta on a task-specific eval set.
- Output: recommended quant profile per workload given a policy (minimize cost subject to latency SLO and quality delta limit).

Key assumptions (editable):
- Baseline model: 70B param variant, FP16 serving baseline.
- Baseline GPU profile: A100-40GB-like performance baseline for FP16. Unit GPU-hour cost: $2.80 (cloud average).
- Tokens per second baseline (FP16): 350 tokens/s for prompt length 128, generation 256.
- Overhead multiplier for network/CPU etc: 1.08 (configurable).
- Quantization multipliers (first-pass heuristics):
  - FP16: cost_multiplier = 1.00, latency_factor = 1.00, quality_delta = 0.0
  - FP8: cost_multiplier = 0.78, latency_factor = 0.95, expected_quality_delta = -0.6%
  - INT8: cost_multiplier = 0.62, latency_factor = 0.85, expected_quality_delta = -1.9%
  - 4-bit: cost_multiplier = 0.42, latency_factor = 0.70, expected_quality_delta = -4.5%
(These are starting heuristics; real numbers must come from microbench + eval suite for each model + hardware combo.)

Definitions and formulae used in the sheet (cells in the spreadsheet):
- effective_throughput = baseline_throughput * (1 / latency_factor) * (1 / overhead_multiplier)
- per_token_gpu_cost = (gpu_hour_cost / 3600) / effective_tokens_per_second
- per_request_cost_example = per_token_gpu_cost * average_response_tokens + per_token_gpu_cost * average_prompt_tokens
- quality_penalty_score = baseline_quality * (1 + expected_quality_delta)  // use absolute or relative depending on metric (e.g., EM vs BLEU vs human NPS)
- normalized_utility = (quality_score_normalized) / per_request_cost  // higher is better

Example calculator rows (workload presets):
- RAG chat (median length): avg_prompt_tokens=180, avg_gen_tokens=220, latency_SLO_ms=600 (p95)
- High-throughput inference (batch embedding): avg_prompt_tokens=64, avg_gen_tokens=0, latency_SLO_ms=200 (p95)
- Low-latency assist (LLM-internal tool): avg_prompt_tokens=90, avg_gen_tokens=40, latency_SLO_ms=250 (p95)

Sample snapshot (numbers illustrative):
- Baseline FP16: throughput 350 t/s, per_token_cost = $0.0000079, per_chat_cost = $0.0029, quality_delta = 0.0
- FP8: throughput 368 t/s, per_token_cost = $0.0000061, per_chat_cost = $0.0022, quality_delta = -0.6%
- INT8: throughput 411 t/s, per_token_cost = $0.0000048, per_chat_cost = $0.0017, quality_delta = -1.9%
- 4-bit: throughput 500 t/s, per_token_cost = $0.0000033, per_chat_cost = $0.0012, quality_delta = -4.5%

Sensitivity scenarios to run (columns to include in sheet):
- Vary quality_delta +/- factor (x0.5, x1, x2) to model fragility of quant to certain prompts.
- Vary SLO: strict (p95 200ms) vs relaxed (p95 1s).
- Vary price of GPU (explore cloud on-demand vs reserved vs dedicated).
- Vary batching window: 10ms/30ms/100ms to see throughput gains vs latency increase.
- Vary cache hit rate for prefix-cache (0%, 25%, 60%).

Decision logic (toy policy implemented as spreadsheet IF statements):
- If (p95_latency_quant_profile <= latency_SLO) AND (quality_delta >= -2.0%) => recommend quant_profile with lowest per_request_cost.
- Else if (p95_latency_quant_profile > latency_SLO) => fallback to lower-latency profile (less quantized) or route to dedicated pool.
- Else if (quality_delta < -2.0%) => mark for human review and A/B test (do not auto-rollout).

Heuristics and rules of thumb to codify:
- Prefer INT8 for RAG-like workloads where retrieval compensates content loss, but validate on F1/NDCG on downstream retrieval-eval sets.
- Avoid 4-bit on high-precision code-completion and summarization tasks unless eval shows <1% quality drop on relevant metrics.
- Use FP8 as a conservative win for latency with minimal quality risk when kernel support exists.

Experimentation plan (short checklist):
- Create microbench harness for each model+hw to measure tokens/s at target seq lengths and batch windows. (owner: eng/inference)
- Run eval suites per workload: generation (ROUGE/BERTScore), code (CodeBLEU), retrieval (Mrr@10/NDCG). (owner: applied-ml)
- Run online A/B for promising profiles with small % of traffic and monitor error-rates, regressions, user visible metrics. (owner: product)
- SLO safety net: auto-fallback routing rule in Redwood Console if p95 latency or error-rate exceeds threshold for 5 min.

Open questions / risks to capture here:
- Kernel maturity: FP8 kernel availability on target GPUs and stable driver stacks.
- Calibration/quant noise: per-layer sensitivity can induce non-linear quality drops that average heuristics miss.
- Latency variability: small-batch tail latency often dominated by IO and CPU preprocessing; quant alone may not fix p95.

Spreadsheet layout (recommended tabs and columns):
- Tab: Inputs (gpu_cost, baseline_throughput, overhead, avg_token_counts, SLOs, batch_window)
- Tab: Microbench (model, hw, seq_len, batch, tokens_s, p50/p95_latency_ms, memory_used)
- Tab: Eval (workload, metric_name, baseline_score, quant_fp8_score, quant_int8_score, quant_4bit_score, delta_pct)
- Tab: Simulator (preset rows, use cell formulas to compute per_token_cost, per_request_cost, p95_estimate, utility_score, recommended_profile)
- Tab: Scenario-scan (sensitivity sweeps / small pivot table for kneepoints)

Quick spreadsheet formulas (example cell formulas explained):
- Cell 'effective_tps' = baseline_tps * (1/latency_factor) * (1/overhead_multiplier)
- Cell 'per_token_cost' = (gpu_hour_cost / 3600) / effective_tps
- Cell 'per_request_cost' = per_token_cost * (avg_prompt_tokens + avg_generation_tokens)
- Cell 'utility' = (baseline_quality - abs(quality_delta)) / per_request_cost  // normalization depends on metric chosen

Guardrails for rollout recommendations (proposed thresholds):
- Auto-recommend: quant profile only if quality_delta >= -1.5% AND p95_latency <= latency_SLO AND per_request_cost_reduction >= 10%
- Soft-recommend (requires A/B): -1.5% > quality_delta >= -3.0% OR per_request_cost_reduction between 5-10%
- Manual review required: quality_delta < -3.0% or per_request_cost_reduction > 30% (suspicious large gaps)

Notes / TODOs (local action items):
- [ ] Hook spreadsheet to microbench CSV export (Jon)
- [ ] Add per-model calibration factors from recent eval (Ravi)
- [ ] Draft console UI mock: include 'recommended quantization' badge per route with explainability points (Elena)

References / links in-line:
- See Microbench harness RFC: confluence:infra-microbench-2025
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/482
- Eval job: JIRA-1987

Comments (freeform):
- This is intentionally a conservative calculator: it tries to avoid auto-rolling riskier quant profiles unless backed by quality data. The goal is to make cost wins explicit and tied to measurable quality and latency constraints so product and SRE can sign off on rollouts.

Author notes: keep the quant multipliers small and editable; the real signal will come from cross-referencing microbench and eval tabs. Prefer a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50%) rather than a single switch.

Last updated by Ava Chen on 2026-02-10.
